_about: Hand-written footnotes on scored weeks, printed under Caveats in that week's scoreboard and in the season summary (tracker/report.py, scoring_notes). They never change a stored result: the official record is the tracker's scoring of nflverse's stats, and decision 17 reads predictions/verification_log.json as logged. A correction nflverse publishes later is caught by check-stats and goes through the normal score --force re-score.

notes.text: **Scoring note (week 8, Jalen Coker):** the official record scores him 10.6 from nflverse's weekly stats, a spike (threshold 10.0). Yahoo scores him 8.6: on CAR's last play he caught a lateral and fumbled, GB recovered, and the league docks 2 for a fumble lost. nflverse's play-by-play charges him with it and its weekly `fumbles_lost_total` counts it, but its receiving, rushing and sack fumble columns, the ones the tracker sums, don't. At 8.6 he is not a spike. In the week's official `thu` run that would change: O.D.D.S. (13-feature) top 10 spike hits 3 to 2 (dart percentile 93 to 79) and top 25 8 to 7 (100 to 99); snap-share heuristic top 25 5 to 4 (89 to 77); dart mean 1.21 to 1.17 (top 10) and 2.99 to 2.85 (top 25); the shadow, last week's points, every under-50% set and the `sun` run (Thursday players are not in its pool) are unchanged. In `verify_week.py`'s record: production precision@10 3/10 to 2/10, @25 8/25 to 7/25, shadow unchanged (4/10, 5/25), QB/RB/WR/TE base rate 37/296 to 36/296. Decision 17's week 8 count stays as logged (production 3, shadow 4; it would read 2 and 4); the rule is applied as written and this note rides alongside. If nflverse corrects the stats, check-stats will flag the week and the normal re-score applies.
